en:
Nice to meet you all.
I'm Shoji Arai, from Class 2-B.
Well then, I'll tell the second story.
Um... what do you all think of the old school building?
I imagine you find it frightening?{p}{f:What|What} about you, {a}?
It's scary
It's not scary
I've never really given it any thought

Yes, I thought so.
That exterior, looking as if it could rot away at any moment.
Just looking at it from a distance, you can feel the danger coming off it.
The old school building, which is now off-limits.{p}

Rounds are necessary, after all.
There's no telling when a thief might break in during the night, and outsiders might start sleeping there without permission.
Though there's nothing in there worth stealing.
So why did even the rounds come to an end?
...There's a reason for that.
That's the story I'll tell you.{p}

Long ago, there was a teacher named Sakurai, but I suppose none of you would know about him.
...He isn't here anymore.
Apparently he was a very good teacher.
They say he was serious and rigid, but he gave his all to everything he did.{p}

Back then, even the teachers hated doing night rounds of the old school building.
Whoever had night duty would find one excuse or another not to patrol the old school building.
Even when they did, they'd just go near it, shine a flashlight around, and call it done.
Even those who meant to go inside would run back the moment that rotted exterior wall loomed faintly in their light.
So on paper, the rounds had been made, but the reality was different.
After all, if even the teachers ran away from it, surely nobody would ever sneak into a place like that.
Everyone told themselves that, to justify the rounds that were never made.
Even so, there was one teacher, and only one, who actually patrolled the old school building.{p}

That was Mr. Sakurai.
It's not that Mr. Sakurai wasn't scared.
If anything, he may have been more easily frightened than most.
Even so, he also had a stronger sense of responsibility than most.
He just couldn't cut corners the way the other teachers did.
There were even people who laughed behind Mr. Sakurai's back for patrolling the old school building so seriously.
Night duty didn't come around very often, but whenever his turn drew near, Mr. Sakurai's heart grew heavy all the same.
And then, once again, his turn for night duty came around.{p}

It was September, yet the day was as sticky and hot as midsummer.
When it's that muggy, you get irritable for no reason.
The sweat pouring from your whole body soaks into your shirt, and the damp shirt clings flat against your skin.
That alone makes the irritation swell unbearably.
It was that kind of day.
Even after nightfall, the temperature showed no sign of dropping, and the heat went on.
A cool breeze might have calmed his irritation a little, but the only wind that blew carried hot, steamy air with it.
With the heat as fierce as ever, the time for the rounds arrived.
The old school building was always the last stop on the rounds.
He would patrol the new school building, the gym, the pool and so on, and finally take on the old school building.
That day, too, apart from the muggy heat, the rounds went along without incident.
He inspected the pool carefully as well, and only the old school building was left.{p}

Suddenly, for no clear reason, Mr. Sakurai felt a chill run down his spine.
He laughed, wondering if it was so muggy that he'd started feeling cold instead.
Even so, the uneasy feeling wouldn't go away.
Something bad was coming; he could feel it.
Maybe he'd better skip the rounds of the old school building today?{p}What should he do?
Do the rounds
Skip the rounds
Go a little later

Mr. Sakurai agonized over it.
Still, he couldn't neglect the rounds he had been assigned.{p}

If something happened because he had skipped them, all the blame would fall on Mr. Sakurai.
When he thought of that, his feet carried him toward the old school building in spite of himself.{p}

The old school building has no electricity.
So however frightened you are, the only thing you can rely on is the single beam of a flashlight lighting your feet.
That day, the light seemed weaker than usual.
Maybe the batteries were running low.
That day of all days, Mr. Sakurai hurried to get the rounds over with.
Despite the heat, for some reason his body wouldn't stop shaking.
Usually he went into each classroom one by one and checked it thoroughly, but that day he simply shone his flashlight in from each doorway and left it at that.{p}

When he had more or less finished checking the three-story old school building, he hurried back to the night-duty room.
Shut up tight as it had been, the night-duty room was like a steam bath.
"...Ugh. I should've left a window open."
Grading the tests he had given that day, Mr. Sakurai thought idly about the old school building.
What had he been so afraid of?
It had been the same as always; nothing at all was different.
No one would ever sneak into an old school building like that.
He was only making the rounds to be ready for that one-in-a-million chance, that was all.
When he finished grading and casually glanced out the window... he saw a faint light mixed in with the darkness.
If he remembered right, in that direction was the old school building...{p}

Could a light be on somewhere in the old school building?
Mr. Sakurai frowned.
That should be impossible.
After all, there was no electricity in the old school building.
And yet, if light was leaking from the old school building, someone must have snuck in.
Someone had snuck in without permission...
Mr. Sakurai reached for the flashlight lying beside him and hurriedly stood up.
But just as he slipped on his sandals to leave the room, he suddenly stopped himself.

What if it was a thief...?
No, what if a vicious criminal who had escaped from prison had fled into that old school building...?

Worrying about things that could never happen... that's human nature.
And precisely because they could never happen, we worry about what we'd do if they did.
Mr. Sakurai agonized.
Would he be all right going alone?{p}Wouldn't it be better to stay right where he was?
Head to the old school building
Stay put and see what happens
Call someone

Mr. Sakurai immediately picked up the receiver.
Before going to check, he figured he would call someone first.
If he let another teacher know, they would surely deal with it properly if anything happened.
...But for some reason, the call wouldn't go through.
There wasn't even a dial tone.
"...That's odd. Is it broken?"
Mr. Sakurai tapped and shook the phone a few times, but the receiver stayed silent.
He followed the phone cord with his eyes, but there was nothing wrong with it.{p}"...Oh, well. It can't be helped."
Head to the old school building
Stay put and see what happens

There were phones in the faculty room, too, and a pay phone as well.
But if some trouble broke out while he was taking his time like this, it would be a disaster.{p}

With that thought, he headed straight for the old school building.
Maybe something else near the old school building was giving off light.
Or maybe he had seen wrong.
Thinking such things, he hurried over at a trot... and what do you know?
A corner of the old school building's second floor was bathed in a hazy light.

"...Someone's in there."
Mr. Sakurai muttered it without thinking, gripped his flashlight tight, and charged into the old school building.{p}

Relying on that feeble light, he climbed the creaking stairs, testing each step so he wouldn't miss his footing.
When he reached the top, Mr. Sakurai couldn't believe his eyes.{p}

The light that had been glowing until a moment ago was out.
The area around the second classroom down from the stairs he had just climbed had definitely been lit.

Mr. Sakurai held his breath.
Whoever had turned on the light must have noticed him coming and hurriedly put it out, he thought.
In that case, he had to act carefully too.
He had no idea who he was dealing with.
If he were caught off guard and attacked from the shadows, he wouldn't stand a chance.{p}

Mr. Sakurai switched off his flashlight.
All at once, total darkness closed in on him.
It drove home to him all over again what a difference even a single flashlight made.
So much so that he caught himself wavering over switching it back on.
Even so, he managed to hold back and swallowed his fear.{p}

There wasn't a single ray of light.
At this angle, not even the moonlight came in.
He had no choice but to grope his way forward in complete darkness.

"Ow!"
Suddenly, a sharp pain shot through his fingertip.
When he touched it, his fingertip was wet and sticky.
He licked it, and it tasted of blood.
When he fearfully reached out again, it seemed he had cut himself on a broken windowpane.{p}

Even in complete darkness, after a while your eyes gradually adjust.
Dimly, he began to make out the shape of the old school building.
Even so, he couldn't move freely.
There were broken windowpanes and old nails sticking out all over the place.
Mr. Sakurai strained his ears.
If someone was there, he should hear a sound.
Even if they were holding their breath too, this was the old school building.
The slightest movement would make the floorboards creak.
He would wait for that moment.
Mr. Sakurai held still and endured.
But no sound came at all.
It was as if there were no one there.{p}

"...Tch. You're a stubborn one."
Clicking his tongue, Mr. Sakurai had no choice but to make the first move himself.

Maybe the floorboards on the second floor were more rotten than on the first; with everything around him so hushed, their creaking echoed all the louder.
With every step he heard a sound like the moaning grudges of people who had died writhing in agony.
The other party showed no sign of moving at all.
Now and then he would stop short and strain his ears, but they just wouldn't give themselves away.{p}

...Was someone really there?
Suddenly, Mr. Sakurai grew uneasy.
And to drown out his own fear, he tried to break the deadlock.{p}He couldn't bear it any longer.
Turn on the flashlight
Shout at the top of his lungs
Stamp loudly on the floor

"Who's there?!
I know someone's in here!"
Unable to stand it, Mr. Sakurai shouted at the top of his lungs.
It was a good thing the school was empty; if he had yelled like that in a residential area, it might have caused an uproar.
That's how loud his voice was.
But no one answered.
"I know you're there!
Come out!
If you come out now, I won't make a big deal out of this!"
Mr. Sakurai bellowed, even louder than before.
The old school building shook as if it were laughing.
Of course, no one answered Mr. Sakurai.
Silence fell once more.
"...I see.
If that's how you want it, I won't go easy on you anymore.
I hope you're ready!"
Mr. Sakurai said that to work up his own courage.
It was almost as if he were asking himself whether he was ready.
And then he began walking slowly toward the classroom where he had seen that light.{p}

That was when it happened.
Mr. Sakurai stopped and listened closely.
Was he hearing things?
...Yes, he must be hearing things.
Then he started walking again.

But once again, he soon stopped.
...Was he hearing things?
Mr. Sakurai just couldn't shake the feeling that he'd heard another set of footsteps.
Each time he took a step, the floorboards creaked along with it.
But slightly out of step with that, he could hear another sound.
The creak, creak of someone treading on the floorboards.

What's more, it was coming from behind him.
Mr. Sakurai shuddered as if ice water had been poured down his back.
When had they gotten behind him?
If he turned around, the intruder at his back might attack him.
He wanted to turn around, but he couldn't.
Instead, he decided to pretend he hadn't noticed and wait for a chance to strike back.
Mr. Sakurai slowly began walking again.{p}
...Creak, creak.
...Creak, creak.
In time with it, he could clearly hear a second set of steps on the floorboards: squeak, squeak.
And it was, without a doubt, coming from behind him.

Mr. Sakurai stopped once more.
And sure enough, the other footsteps stopped too.
...There was no doubt about it.
The intruder was behind him.
Mr. Sakurai was certain of it.{p}Now, should he just whirl around and lunge at whoever it was...?
Turn around and lunge at them
Turn around and switch on the flashlight
Don't turn around; stay put and see what happens

"Who's there?!"
The instant he turned, Mr. Sakurai aimed the flashlight where the intruder's face ought to be and switched it on.
The glare was so bright that Mr. Sakurai himself had to squint.
For a moment he was dazzled, but when he quickly strained his eyes... there was no one there.{p}

"...That's strange."
Mr. Sakurai tilted his head, then slowly stepped toward the spot his light was shining on.

That was when it happened.
The other footsteps started up again.{p}
...From right behind Mr. Sakurai.
Startled, Mr. Sakurai stopped in his tracks.

And then the other footsteps stopped too.
When had they slipped around behind him?
Mr. Sakurai couldn't stop the hand gripping the flashlight from shaking violently.

Even so, he had to find out.
If whoever it was really was behind him, he had to find out, no matter what.
Driven by that sense of duty, Mr. Sakurai gulped down the spit that had pooled in his mouth.{p}But it was also true that he was scared, scared out of his wits.
Turn around
Run away without turning around
"Come out! Come out, I said!"{p}
Mr. Sakurai turned around and swung the flashlight about wildly.{p}

...But the single thin beam of light showed him nothing at all.
"Where are you?!"{p}

Mr. Sakurai stomped all over the floor, deliberately making his footsteps loud, and walked around with no aim at all.
And would you believe it, the footsteps followed right along with him.
Whenever Mr. Sakurai walked, he heard the footsteps.
What's more, the other footsteps matched his own exactly, every bit as loud.
Always from behind him...
And whenever he stopped walking, the footsteps stopped dead too, as if they were reading Mr. Sakurai's mind.{p}

"Hah... hah..."
At last Mr. Sakurai was worn out, his shoulders heaving with every breath.
His face was drenched with sweat.
Not so much from the muggy heat; it was cold sweat.
...Squeak, squeak.

...Squeak, squeak.{p}Mr. Sakurai focused every nerve on his ears.
Can you believe it?
The other footsteps were coming from behind him.
Even though he was standing still.
He couldn't hear his own footsteps, and yet now he could clearly hear the other footsteps, and only them.
And the distance, which had stayed more or less the same, began closing, closer and closer.
As the gap closed, he felt as if a cold wind were blowing on him from behind.

And at last the footsteps stopped dead, as if they had nestled right up against Mr. Sakurai's back.
The cold was like sticking his face into a freezer.
Something was definitely behind him.
Something that wasn't human...
Right now, he felt, he might be able to see it.
Should he turn around and look?
Or should he break into a run and escape?{p}He had only two choices left now.
Turn around
Run away

As he whirled around, Mr. Sakurai pointed the flashlight.
And there...{p}

"AAAAAAAAAAAAAGH!"
Mr. Sakurai's scream echoed through the school in the middle of the night.{p}

...It was the next morning
when they found Mr. Sakurai, wandering aimlessly and unsteadily across the schoolyard.
With the flashlight still switched on, he was staggering round and round the schoolyard like a drunk.
Drool dribbled slackly from his mouth, his hair had turned pure white, and his face had aged as if he'd grown thirty years older all at once.
And,
"...It is my friend.
...And I am its friend.
...Let's all die together.
...Let's die happily."
he was singing, so they say, to an eerie little tune.{p}

Mr. Sakurai was admitted to a hospital for treatment.
The treatment isn't making much progress, and I hear there's almost no hope of recovery.
And they say he still hums that song even now...
What on earth did Mr. Sakurai see?
Did he see something truly horrifying, I wonder?
And is that thing still lurking in the old school building, even now?
If the old school building gets torn down soon...
what on earth will become of it?
...My story ends here.
Thank you very much.{p}

I see. Then you won't mind the story you're about to hear.
Good, good.
Then I can tell it without holding anything back.
It's about that old school building...{p}

I see.
This might actually be good.
You won't have any preconceptions, so it'll be worth telling you a scary story.
Old wooden buildings are, how should I put it, brittle, or musty, or dusty, aren't they?
That stale old smell lies there dozing, and when you rattle the door open, the air inside comes rushing out at you, doesn't it?
I hate that.
Doesn't it feel like a different world?
The old school building is like that too, I'd say.
Oh, no, I've never actually been inside it.
It's been many years since the old school building stopped being used, but the teachers did at least keep patrolling it.
And there's a story about one of those teachers' patrols...{p}

Back then, there was a student teacher named Ms. Sasaki, I hear.
Student teachers usually go back to their old school to do their training, don't they?
Ms. Sasaki, too, had been coming to school in this school's uniform only a few years before.
No one would ever make a student teacher do the night patrols of the school, right?
But that year, of all years, a spiteful teacher pushed to have her do it.{p}

Of course, she wasn't supposed to do it alone.
"Good luck tonight, Ms. Sasaki.
Ho ho ho."
"You make it sound so easy..."
No matter how old you get, your seniors are always mean.
That was what Ms. Sasaki thought.
"Just my luck. This year of all years, we have to patrol the old school building too. This is the worst."
Back in her student days, she'd been in the tennis club.
She found herself remembering the stories about the old school building that she'd heard at a ghost-story session during training camp.
"It's bringing back all kinds of memories...
Honestly, you seniors... I'm going to hold this against you."
That day there was supposed to be one more teacher on night duty, but there had been a death in that teacher's family, and they suddenly had to go home.
So Ms. Sasaki ended up doing the patrol all by herself.
"Well, if it's come to this, I might as well just brave it out.
Grumble, grumble..."
The old school building was three stories tall, and of course it had no electricity.
"Why do they keep this building around forever?
And up close, it looks even more dreadful."
Complaining all the while, Ms. Sasaki went inside.{p}

I think part of her wanted to see something scary, too.
The place was off-limits, so she must have been curious about it.
Ms. Sasaki was the nosy type, easily carried away by anything exciting.
She was still a college girl back then, after all.{p}
She decided to go up to the third floor first, then work her way down floor by floor.
Relying on the feeble light of her flashlight, she climbed the stairs, creak, creak, testing each step so she wouldn't miss her footing.{p}

When she pointed the flashlight at a window, she saw her own faint reflection in the thin glass.
As she stared at it, she felt as though another shadow were overlapping her reflection, and she couldn't help jerking the flashlight away.{p}

"I was acting tough, but I really do feel scared and alone..."
Then, done with the third floor, she went down to the second.{p}

"The second floor is in much worse shape."
When she shone the light into the classrooms, she could see broken window glass and old nails sticking out all over the place.{p}

As she made her way forward, crunching the thin scattered glass underfoot, crack, crack,
"Huh?"

Her body wouldn't move forward.
"Hey, come on, you're joking, right?"
It felt like something had hold of her.
"Let go of me, let go, I said☆
Ugh, if you don't let go, you're getting this☆"{p}

There was a ripping sound, something tearing.
"Huh..."
She had gotten caught on a protruding nail and had been struggling against it.
"How awful!
This blouse cost a fortune!
Argh, I'm so mad!"
It was her own fault for jumping to conclusions, but she conveniently ignored that and sulked, I'm told.{p}

She hurried down the stairs, and was just about to head along the long first-floor corridor when...
"?"
She could hear something.
A child was laughing.

What's more, it sounded like a baby.
"Ahahaha, hee-hee-hee..."{p}

Again, she hurriedly turned to face forward.
The laughter came closer and closer.
From behind her.

"What do I do?
Why would there be a baby laughing in the old school building?
No, no, no, it's getting closer☆
What do I do?
Why★
This isn't fair!
Why is this happening?!☆"
She was in a total panic.
"Don't turn around, whatever you do☆"
Just as she murmured that, as if telling herself, the baby leapt and latched onto her back.{p}

"Ahahaha, ah-ah-ah, ah-hah!"
The baby laughed on her right shoulder.
"Eeek☆"
People are strange in moments like this. You know you should leave well enough alone, yet you end up doing the exact opposite of what you should.
She, too, glanced at her right shoulder without thinking.{p}

"Gyaaaaah☆"
Suddenly the baby, its eyes rolled back to the whites, leapt from her shoulder onto the nape of her neck.
"Ahahaha, ah-ah-ah, ah-hah!"
She says she doesn't remember what happened after that.{p}

The next morning, she was found at the entrance of the old school building, laughing like a baby,
"Ahahaha, ah-ah-ah, ah-hah!"
and sucking on her fingers.
I heard this later: some time before, a newborn baby had been abandoned in the old school building.
Yes, by the time it was found, the baby was no longer breathing.
Apparently, if it had been found sooner, it might have been saved.
The teacher who had neglected the patrol back then came in for a lot of criticism.{p}

What became of her?
I hear she's recovered from the shock and is doing fine now.
Naturally, she gave up on becoming a teacher. She's an ordinary office worker now.
She says she still dreams about that baby sometimes.
How do I know all this?
Well, Ms. Sasaki is the young woman who lives next door to my family.
...And that's the end of my story.
Thank you very much.{p}

That's right. I always patrol the old building properly, so surely heaven won't punish me for skipping it just once.
None of the other teachers take it seriously anyway, so it shouldn't matter.
That's what Mr. Sakurai tried to tell himself, but being conscientious to the core, he couldn't bring himself to decide.
It reminded him that this personality of his had always made him lose out, ever since he was young.
How should I put it... he just wasn't savvy. You know how it is: there are kids who barely study yet still get good scores on tests, and kids who study three times as hard as everyone else and somehow never score very well, right?
Yes, Mr. Sakurai was the second kind.
You can sort of picture it, can't you?{p}

Mr. Sakurai was about to drink some barley tea and take a breather.
"Whoa, lightning, huh... That startled me."

The sky had flashed, and thunder began to rumble.
"Hm, fifteen seconds between the flash and the sound.
It's quite far off.
Maybe I'd better finish the patrol before the rain starts..."
He trotted off toward the old school building.{p}

He stepped inside quietly and listened hard.
"I don't seem to hear anything."

Relying on the feeble light of his flashlight, he climbed the stairs, creak, creak, testing each step so he wouldn't miss his footing.
When he reached the top, Mr. Sakurai couldn't believe his eyes.{p}

"For now, I'll just stay put and see what happens."
Mr. Sakurai stared out the window without moving a muscle.
As he kept still, sweat broke out all over his face.
Then the sweat ran down his chin and dripped off.
But the longer he stayed like this, the more his imagination kept turning to the worst...
Mr. Sakurai was a worrier, and he just couldn't stop fretting about it.
"As long as I'm the one on patrol, I have to do it properly, or I'll set a poor example."{p}

Mr. Sakurai stayed still for a while in the muggy night-duty room.
But even if there was an intruder, would they stay in the old building? And what would he do if they snuck into the new building too?
That's right, it was definitely better to settle this while the intruder was still in the old building.
He had to stop them before the damage spread.{p}

When he switched on the flashlight, light suddenly spread across his view, and a sense of relief spread through him.
But then anxiety spread again, as if to wipe that relief away.
"This is practically telling them where I am."
But if he turned the flashlight off, he'd be in trouble if anything happened.
Just then, sensing something behind him,{p}
Mr. Sakurai stomped on the floor as hard as he could.
"...Oh no!"

His foot went right through the hallway floor.
When he tried to pull it out, the broken, jagged splinters of wood stabbed into it.
Blood was already seeping from where his leg had been cut when it broke through the floor.
But unless he got it out somehow, he'd be stuck here, unable to move, and then he'd be helpless.
He struggled.{p}

When he happened to look up, he saw something hazy at the far end of the hallway.
"Smoke?"
Now that he thought about it, he felt he'd been smelling something smoky for a while.
But the haze didn't seem to be smoke.
Even though his flashlight wasn't on, he could see that one spot clearly.
When he looked closer, something seemed to be writhing inside it.
And it seemed to be coming slowly toward him.
"An intruder?"{p}

He struggled to pull his foot free, but it only made the wound worse; the more he panicked, the more stuck it seemed to get.
Then he looked toward the far end of the hallway again.{p}

This time he could see it clearly.
It was obviously a person.

It seemed to be crawling toward him.
Why would a person be crawling around the old school building...?
Maybe this wasn't a human at all?
The nasty thought crossed his mind.
Mind you, I wouldn't want it to be a real human either.
While he was thinking that, it drew closer and closer.
Slither, slither, slither, drag... drag, slither, slither, slither...
On a closer look, it seemed to be a man.
It was grinning, and every so often it would stop, open its eyes wide, and stare right at him.
Trapped and with nothing left he could do, the teacher{p}

"Ngh☆"
squeezed his eyes shut and curled himself up tight, not moving.
...It felt as though some time had passed since then.
"Strange... nothing's happening..."
He fearfully opened his eyes.{p}

He switched on the flashlight in his hand and lit up his feet.
"This is bad, look at all this blood..."
Then, the moment he tried to yank his foot out of the hole with all his might, it popped out with surprising ease.
Carried by his own force, he tumbled backward and crashed into a pillar.
"Ow, ow... When it rains, it pours."
And just as he was about to get up, the grinning man from before was peering down at him from directly above.{p}
"Eep☆"
He couldn't even scream, nor could he tear his eyes away from the man's face.

One moment the man was grinning, and the next his eyes flew wide open and he stared at the teacher.
Those eyes were far larger than a normal person's, and murky, and the whites were shot through with swollen red capillaries.
Suddenly, the thing pushed its face close.
And its face came closer, and closer.{p}
"Eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee☆"{p}

The next morning, Mr. Sakurai was found in the hallway of the old school building.
I hear he was crawling back and forth along the hallway on all fours, laughing.
Mr. Sakurai was admitted to a hospital for treatment.
The treatment has made little progress, and they say there's almost no hope of recovery.{p}

I heard this later: long ago, when the old school building was still in use, there was once a small fire.
Even though it was only a small fire, the custodian had the bad luck to be overcome by the smoke, and died.
Apparently the custodian suffered from a bronchial condition, so breathing in the smoke must have brought on an attack.
I imagine he tried desperately to avoid the smoke and get away by keeping low to the floor.{p}

What Mr. Sakurai saw was probably the custodian's ghost.
Perhaps he resented losing his life in what was only a small fire.
Oh, that reminds me, they say the old school building will be torn down soon.
I hope nothing happens...
...That's the end of my story.
Thank you.{p}

"Oh, here goes nothing!"
Mr. Sakurai spun around and leapt straight at it.
"Ugh☆"
There was definitely someone standing there.
Mr. Sakurai had the figure locked tight in his arms.
He had never expected the intruder to be exactly where he'd guessed, so he was startled, and at the same time froze where he was.
The thing was scrawnier than he'd expected, and seemed to be wearing something damp, stiff and musty-smelling.
"This could be the end!
I'm done for!
...?"
Eerily, the thing did nothing...
Both the teacher and the thing held that position, motionless, for a while.{p}

As they stayed like that, he gradually felt it start to hug him back.
"Wh-what are you doing☆"{p}

It squeezed tighter and tighter.
It hurt; he couldn't breathe.
In the end, the tremendous strength felt like it would make his spine crack.
Where could such a scrawny body get strength like this?
"Gwaaaaargh!"
In his agony, the teacher moved his head, knowing he had to see the intruder's face.
But no matter what he did, he couldn't see its face.
All he could see was ragged hair streaked with white.
Then the intruder's face swiveled around toward him.{p}

"☆"
The teacher froze, as if someone had dropped ice down his back.
The intruder's face was a bare skull.
What's more, the skull was staring at him resentfully with eyes that didn't seem to focus.
"Warm me...
I'm cold...
I have nowhere to go..."
The teacher fainted on the spot.{p}

Come to think of it, they say Mr. Sakurai's body temperature never rises as high as a normal person's, and he's always shivering.
I heard this later: long ago, this area was an old battlefield.
Maybe the restless spirit of someone killed in that fighting, one that never passed on, envied Mr. Sakurai's warm-blooded body and came out.
People who can see them see them, apparently... They say this school is crawling with more spirits than you could ever imagine.
...That's the end of my story.
Thank you.{p}

For now, the teacher decided to stay as he was and see what happened, listening intently.
He thought that might be the wiser choice...
He couldn't hear the intruder make a sound; all he could hear was the window glass rattling in the wind and the beating of his own heart.
He even felt as if the intruder's breathing were drifting toward him on the air around him.
The intruder, somewhere out of sight, no doubt staring hard at his back...
(Are they waiting for me to make the first move after all?)
Behind him, he could sense the intruder, or maybe he couldn't...
In that murky, uncertain atmosphere, Mr. Sakurai could only stand there, not knowing what to do.
His hands were damp with greasy sweat.
"I'm not getting anywhere like this..."{p}

That was when it happened.
Without meaning to, the teacher dropped the flashlight he was holding.

"Oh no!"
The jolt of the fall seemed to have switched the flashlight on.
"Well, if it's come to this..."
Mr. Sakurai hurriedly snatched it up,{p}

"Ah!"
His foot caught on a piece of wood, and he fell.
"Grrrrr..."
He felt furious at his own rotten luck.
"F-fine, I'll just go for broke!"{p}

Mr. Sakurai broke into a dash.
"If I turn at the end of that hall and go down the stairs, I should see the exit right away!"
He had come in sandals, so shards of glass had gotten in and cut his feet, but he couldn't worry about that now.
"That corner, if I can just get around that corner☆"
He felt as if those footsteps were chasing after him too.{p}
And he turned at the end of the hall and ran down the stairs.
But just then, something slammed into his back with a thud.

"Waaaaaaaaaaaaaah!"
With a horrible crash, Mr. Sakurai tumbled down the stairs...
As he drifted in and out of consciousness, Mr. Sakurai saw it.
A male student standing at the top of the stairs, laughing as he looked down at him...
And the teacher clearly heard what the student said.
"You're the same as me... hm hm hm."{p}

The next morning, Mr. Sakurai was found collapsed at the foot of the stairs in the old school building.
I hear he'd rolled over glass and wood chips, so he was badly hurt and needed many stitches.
After he got out of the hospital, Mr. Sakurai quit teaching.
They say a stain like a handprint stayed on his back and never faded.{p}

I wonder what that male student was.
I hear the old school building will be torn down soon, but I can't shake the feeling that something's going to happen.
...That's the end of my story.
Thank you.{p}
